summary: Clarifies and updates a single sentence in RFC 3979 about third-party intellectual property disclosures. When someone else files a disclosure, the IETF Executive Director is to notify the IPR holder and ask whether they have any disclosure to make. It is a best current practice, later replaced by RFC 8179.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4879 clarifies who should be asked for a licensing assurance when someone else files an intellectual property disclosure. The IETF Executive Director is to ask the rights holder, not the person who made the disclosure.

subtitle: A one-word clarification to the third-party IPR disclosure process.

tldr.problem: RFC 3979 asked the IETF Executive Director to request a licensing assurance from the discloser, even when a third party had filed the disclosure.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4879 changes the word discloser to holder in Section 4(C), directing the request to the holder of the intellectual property rights.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4879 is a Best Current Practice, updates RFC 3979, and was obsoleted by RFC 8179.

today: RFC 4879 is a Best Current Practice and was obsoleted by RFC 8179, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: Third-Party Disclosures
sections.content: RFC 4879 clarifies and updates one sentence in RFC 3979 about third-party intellectual property rights (IPR) disclosures. When a third party files a disclosure, the IETF Executive Director is to notify the IPR holder and ask whether the holder has a disclosure to make under the applicable rules.
sections.plainLanguage: Someone other than the rights holder may file a disclosure. The Executive Director tells the holder and asks whether they have a disclosure to make.

sections.title: Changing Discloser to Holder
sections.content: Section 4(C) of RFC 3979 says the Executive Director requests a written licensing assurance from the discloser. RFC 4879 explains that a third-party discloser does not own the rights and cannot speak for their licensing terms. It therefore changes the word discloser to holder in that sentence.
sections.plainLanguage: A person who reports someone else's rights cannot promise how those rights may be licensed. The request should go to the rights holder.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that it has no known security implications. It changes a sentence in an administrative procedure about who is asked for a licensing assurance.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC says it has no known security implications. Its change clarifies an administrative request.
